posts.title: Another New Door Handle
posts.description: How much does it cost to fix a broken door handle in 2026 on a 2013 Model S? I replaced the driver side door handle for $506.24 with mobile service that took one hour. The appointment wait time was three weeks. The original two week appointment was canceled as the service technician was ill that day. I experimented with several different methods to get in and out of the car as the broken door handle was the driver’s door. Three options exist from least desirable to most desirable. Open another door and crawl into the driver’s seat Go into the back of the car and lean over and either roll down the window or open the door from the back. When exiting the car roll down the window! This option works well when it is not raining and have nothing of any value in your car. You can then just grab the interior door handle to open the car door. posts.title: Rivian Suspension – EV Replacement Part II
posts.description: It has been a few months since I wrote the original post about replacing my Model S. During this time my decisions have drastically changed! I subsequently test drove the Polestar 4 and really liked it except for the rear view mirror. Not so much because it is a digital screen but that it is a little too close to the driver’s head. For those of us who need mild reading glasses, the screen could be an issue. But my biggest concern was that the local store was pulling out requiring me to drive about an hour a way to buy the car. If they can’t manage to find a location and sell enough in Silicon Valley to be profitable, I find that situation troubling. As I mentioned in the first post I drove a few Rivians but I was not very happy with the suspension on the R1S. The R1T was fine after an extended test drive, but I couldn’t fit it into the garage nor charge it easily without modification of the charging setup. posts.title: EV Replacement
posts.description: I am starting to explore the next car to replace my 2013 Model S 85kWh battery with 145,000 miles. I could easily buy a car right now, wait till the Model S is a brick, or worst case buy one at the end of 2026 when the current tires will likely be at the end of their useful life. I’ve been researching cars for over a month and have visited many dealers, watched too many videos, read a lot of car reviews and owner feedback on various online forums. I’m completely stuck at the moment now as there aren’t any current cars that fit enough of my needs to replace the Model S. With a couple of new cars (BMW iX3) on the horizon for 2026, I would rather hold out at the moment to evaluate them when available in the U.S. The current value of my car either as a trade in or take away ranges from $4,500 to $6,000 (most likely for the parts).
